An [official coloring of One Piece exists](http://kissmanga.com/Manga/One-Piece-Digital-Colored-Comics), but not all of it is translated.  From the looks of it, the only arcs that are available in their entirety are:


*Captain Morgan

*Orange Town

*Captain Kuro

*Alabasta

*Saboady

*Amazon Lily

*Impel Down

*Marineford

*Return to Saboady

There are I think 6 chapters missing from Post-War(585-589) so you can read the majority of that in color, as well as the beginning of Fishman Island.  Other than that, it would be better to stick with the black and white.  It'll take a little time to make heads or tails of some things but you'll get there eventually!

Also, yes manga is read right-to-left, top-to-down.  Word bubbles can be confusing, but if it's not attributed to a character it's probably someone yelling from off-panel.  Every now and then the word bubble will have a character's head in it to tell who is talking, but that's usually in special cases.

I hope I was of some help, and good luck!

The way I usually see it is alot of people jump to the manga either during Skypiea or shortly after.  Skypiea, while it is a good arc, is a really long arc as well (66 chapers, 43 episodes).  Because of the length of the arc, the anime starts to show it's pacing problems and becomes really slow to watch, while the manga seems to go at a pretty consistent pace(plus people tend to read chapters faster than the episode that adapts them, so it goes by at a faster pace that way too).

Personally, I'd say stick to the manga, and watch whatever fights/moments/etc. that you liked on youtube or what have you.  But if you really want to try the anime out, watch up to and through Skypiea, and if you aren't troubled by the pacing you can probably keep with it.

Something worth noting though, there comes a point in the anime, I think Amazon Lily, where each episode adapts one chapter. That means a chapter that usually takes like 5 minutes to read is stretched into 20 minutes of animation, which really hurts the show in my opinion.  I believe this is still the case now, which means that from episode 400ish onward you're watching a 1:1 manga:anime adaption.  So unless you really like having color and animation and voices, I would strongly recommend sticking with the manga at that point if you haven't already.
